title: Greeting to the Church in Smyrna
english: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the church of God the Father and of the beloved Jesus Christ, which is in Smyrna in Asia. This church has been shown mercy in every gift, has been filled with faith and love, is lacking in no gift, is most befitting God and bearer of holiness. I rejoice greatly in a blameless spirit and in the word of God.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Smyrna with a formal greeting, identifying himself and blessing the church.

title: Christ's real flesh, Davidic descent, and cross
english: I glorify Jesus Christ, the God who has made you so wise. For I have understood that you are fitted together in an unshakable faith, as if nailed to the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ in both flesh and spirit, and grounded in love by the blood of Christ. You are fully assured about our Lord, who is truly of the family of David according to the flesh, Son of God by the will and power of God, truly born of a virgin, baptized by John so that all righteousness might be fulfilled by him.

He was truly nailed in the flesh for us under Pontius Pilate and Herod the tetrarch. We are the fruit of his divinely blessed passion, so that he might raise a sign for the ages through the resurrection for his holy and faithful ones, whether among Jews or among Gentiles, in one body of his church.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the Smyrnaeans by praising God for their firm faith and rehearsing the true facts of Christ's incarnation, baptism, crucifixion, and resurrection.

title: Christ truly suffered, not in mere appearance
english: He suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved. And he truly suffered, just as he truly raised himself. It is not as some faithless people say, that he suffered only in mere appearance. They themselves are unreal, and as they think, so it will happen to them, since they are bodiless and demonic.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, warning against teachers who deny the real flesh and suffering of Jesus Christ.

title: The Risen Christ Truly Flesh
english: For I know and believe that he was in the flesh even after the resurrection.

And when he came to those around Peter, he said to them: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon." And immediately they touched him and believed, being joined to his flesh and his spirit. For this reason they also despised death, and they proved to be beyond death.
After the resurrection he ate and drank with them as one who is fleshly, even though he was spiritually united to the Father.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, refuting those who say Christ only seemed to suffer, and here he gives his own testimony about the risen Christ.

title: Warning against human-shaped beasts and the reality of his bonds
english: I urge these things on you, beloved, knowing that you too hold the same conviction. But I am guarding you in advance against the beasts in human form. You must not only refuse to welcome them; if possible, do not even meet them. Only pray for them, in case they might somehow repent, though that is difficult. Yet Jesus Christ, our true life, has power over this.

For if these things were done by our Lord in mere appearance, then I too am bound in mere appearance. And why have I handed myself over to death, to fire, to the sword, to beasts? No: to be near the sword is to be near God; to be among beasts is to be among God. Only in the name of Jesus Christ do I endure everything, so that I may suffer with him, since the perfect man empowers me.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Smyrnaeans, warning them against false teachers who deny the real flesh of Christ, and now turns to his own imprisonment as proof that Christ's suffering was real.

title: Deniers of Christ's flesh carry a corpse
english: Some people deny him because they do not know him. Or rather, they have been denied by him, because they are advocates of death rather than of the truth. The prophecies did not persuade them, nor did the law of Moses, nor even to this day the gospel, nor our own individual sufferings.

For they think the same way about us as well. What good does it do me if someone praises me but blasphemes my Lord by refusing to confess that he bore flesh? The one who says this has completely denied him and is a bearer of death.
I did not think it right to write down their names, since they are faithless. But may I never even remember them until they repent concerning the passion, which is our resurrection.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Smyrnaeans against teachers who deny that Christ truly suffered and rose in the flesh, and he now describes their denial and his refusal even to name them.

title: No one should be deceived: judgment awaits even heavenly powers without faith in Christ's blood
english: Let no one be deceived. Even the heavenly things, the glory of the angels, and the rulers both visible and invisible: if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, judgment awaits them as well. Let the one who can receive this receive it. Let no one be puffed up by position, for the whole matter is faith and love, and nothing is preferred above these.

But take careful note of those who hold different opinions about the grace of Jesus Christ that has come to us, and see how contrary they are to the mind of God. They have no care for love, none for the widow, none for the orphan, none for the afflicted, none for the one who is bound or the one who is free, none for the one who hungers or thirsts.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Smyrnaeans against false teachers, saying that even heavenly beings face judgment unless they believe in the blood of Christ, and that no position should make anyone proud.

title: Abstain from those who deny the Eucharist
english: They abstain from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they do not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, the flesh that suffered for our sins and that the Father raised up in his goodness. So those who speak against the gift of God die in their disputing. It would have been better for them to love, so that they might also rise.

It is fitting to abstain from such people and not to speak about them either privately or publicly, but to attend to the prophets and especially to the gospel, in which the passion has been made clear to us and the resurrection has been brought to completion. Flee divisions as the beginning of evils.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Smyrnaeans against teachers who deny the real flesh of Christ, and now he turns to their practice of staying away from the Eucharist and prayer.

title: Follow the bishop as Christ follows the Father
english: All of you follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ followed the Father, and follow the council of elders as you would the apostles. Respect the deacons as God's command. Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop or under someone he has entrusted.

Wherever the bishop appears, there let the congregation be, just as wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the whole church. It is not permitted to baptize or to hold a love-feast without the bishop. But whatever he approves, this is also pleasing to God, so that everything you do may be secure and valid.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to do nothing apart from the bishop and to regard only the Eucharist celebrated under the bishop's authority as valid.

title: Honor the bishop; God will repay
english: It is good for us now to come to our senses, while we still have time to repent and turn to God. It is good to know God and the bishop. Whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God. Whoever does anything in secret from the bishop serves the devil.

So let everything abound among you in grace, for you are worthy of it. You have refreshed me in every way, and Jesus Christ will refresh you. You loved me both when I was absent and when I was present. God is your reward: through him, enduring all things, you will obtain him.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Smyrnaeans, urging them to use the remaining time for repentance and to honor the bishop, and promising that God will reward their love shown to him.

title: Thanks for receiving Philo and Rheus Agathopus
english: You did well to receive Philo and Rheus Agathopus as deacons of God. They followed me for the sake of the word of God, and they give thanks to the Lord for you, because you refreshed them in every way. Nothing will be lost to you at all.
My spirit is a ransom for you, and my bonds as well, which you did not despise or feel ashamed of. Nor will the perfect hope, Jesus Christ, be ashamed of you.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Smyrnaeans, thanking them for receiving two companions who followed him for the sake of God's word.

title: Send a delegate to Antioch to rejoice with the restored church
english: Your prayer reached the church in Antioch of Syria. From there I greet you all, bound as I am in chains most worthy of God. I am not worthy to come from that place, for I am the least of them. Yet by God's will I was counted worthy, not because of my own conscience but by the grace of God. I pray that this grace may be given to me in full, so that through your prayer I may attain God.

So that your work may be complete both on earth and in heaven, it is fitting for the honor of God that your church appoint a godly ambassador. He should go to Syria and rejoice with the church there, because they are at peace, have received back their own greatness, and their own body has been restored to them.

It seemed to me, then, a thing worthy of God to send one of your own with a letter, so that he might join in glorifying the calm that has come to them from God, and because they have already reached harbor through your prayer. Since you are perfect, think perfect things. For God is ready to grant you well-being.
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the Smyrnaeans, has just praised them for receiving his companions and now asks them to send a representative to the church in Antioch, which has regained peace.

title: Greetings from Troas and blessing on the Smyrnaeans
english: The love of the brothers in Troas greets you. I am writing to you from there through Burrhus, whom you sent with me together with the Ephesians, your brothers. He refreshed me in every way. I wish everyone would imitate him, for he is an example of God's service. Grace will repay him in every way.

I greet the bishop who is worthy of God, the council of elders that befits God, my fellow servants the deacons, and everyone both individually and together, in the name of Jesus Christ and in his flesh and blood, in his passion and resurrection, both in flesh and in spirit, in the unity of God and of you. Grace, mercy, peace, and endurance be yours through all things.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the church in Smyrna, sending greetings from the brothers in Troas and blessing the Smyrnaean church in the name of Jesus Christ.

title: Final greetings to Smyrnaean households
english: I greet the households of my brothers and sisters, together with their wives and children, and the virgins who are called widows. Be strong for me in the power of the Father. Philo, who is with me, greets you.

I greet the household of Tavia, and I pray that she may be established in faith and love, both fleshly and spiritual. I greet Alce, the name I long for, and Daphnus the incomparable, and Eutecnus, and everyone by name. Be strong in the grace of God.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the church in Smyrna, sending personal greetings to households and named individuals.
